html:
SMTO-OBS-0002 — SMTO couldn't find the activity record for this run

GUID: b08898ae-5232-4a03-af32-a69c581b299b
Slug: trace-not-found
Domain: OBS · Subsystem: obs

What happened

  • The step-by-step record for this run isn't in SMTO's saved history. It may have been deleted with its conversation, or your page is pointing at an old run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the page, then open the conversation and the reply for this run again. An open page can still point at a run that has since been replaced or removed; reloading shows the current list.
  2. If the conversation was deleted, or removed by Auto-purge in Settings › Data, its activity record is gone for good. Deleting a conversation also deletes the activity records of its runs.
  3. To find out what the run did, check what it produced, such as files or messages, instead of starting it again. A missing record doesn't show whether the work happened, so starting again could repeat it.

What success looks like

  • The run's activity opens and lists its steps.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't keep using an old link to this run; it points to a record that no longer exists.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • AgentTraceStore could not find the requested trace in memory or durable storage, or the request was tombstoned as deleted, while waiting for or reading its events.

What this means

  • Trace lookup/wait cannot find the requested trace in retained storage. Observation is read-only and scoped to retained evidence. Missing, ambiguous or incomplete presentation cannot prove that external work failed or never happened; no diagnostic reconstructs or replays it.

Why this can happen

  • Trace lookup/wait cannot find the requested trace in retained storage.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the request identity with the current run list and retention state.

How to fix it

  • Refresh the run list and use a current request_id; the trace may have been deleted with its conversation, tombstoned, or removed by retention. If retention removed it, use the remaining authoritative receipts in the native run store rather than reconstructing missing trace events.
  • Refresh the run list and open a current trace identity. If retention removed it, use the remaining authoritative receipts rather than reconstructing missing evidence.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A current trace or remaining authoritative receipts provide the available evidence.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Observation is read-only and scoped to retained evidence. Missing, ambiguous or incomplete presentation cannot prove that external work failed or never happened; no diagnostic reconstructs or replays it.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
